articles.title: R Madhavan, Vijay Deverakonda, Ravi Kishan and Paresh Rawal hail pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for saving 174 people on a flydubai flight
articles.summary: Several film personalities, including R Madhavan, Shilpa Shetty, Vijay Deverakonda, Ravi Kishan and Paresh Rawal, have applauded Indian pilot Captain Smit
articles.body: Several film personalities, including R Madhavan, Shilpa Shetty, Vijay Deverakonda, Ravi Kishan and Paresh Rawal, have applauded Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his bravery. He allegedly stopped his co-pilot from crashing a Flydubai flight that carried 174 passengers, 27 of them children.R Madhavan and Vijay Deverakonda lead the tributesR Madhavan shared Prime Minister Narendra Modi's statement on the incident and wished the captain a speedy recovery. He called him "a true hero."Vijay praised the pilot's calm in a life-threatening situation. "May God protect you and bless you, Captain. What you faced and what you did is incredible. Along with everyone else on that flight," he wrote.Ravi Kishan, Paresh Rawal and others reactActor-politician Ravi Kishan spoke of the captain's dedication and strength. "Captain Smit Machchhar is the epitome of unwavering loyalty to duty, indomitable courage, and extraordinary wisdom (sic)," he wrote, adding that the pilot's actions are a matter of great national pride.Paresh Rawal played on the pilot's surname, recalling a well-known dialogue by Nana Patekar from the 1994 film 'Krantiveer'. "Remembering NANA PATEKAR'S FAMOUS DIALOGUE: Ek Machhhar Aadmiko...!" he posted.Shilpa Shetty also extended her support to those affected. "Heart goes out to everyone affected. And immense respect for Captain Smit Machchhar for bringing over 170 lives to safety," she wrote.Jackie Shroff paid tribute to the captain and everyone who helped avoid the disaster. “Some heroes work in silence! All my respects to Captain Smit Machchhar and the other brave heroes for saving lives and averting a massive tragedy," he said.PM Narendra Modi's messageAlong with Narendra Modi, actors Sonam Kapoor and Kangana Ranaut also took to social media to appreciate the pilot. The Prime Minister tweeted, “Captain Smit Machchhar has shown the world the highest form of courage. Without fearing for his own life, he fought valiantly and prevented another 9/11-like attack from happening. 140 crore Indians salute Captain Smit and are praying for his well-being."What happened on the flightThe flydubai flight was headed from Dubai to Tel Aviv but was diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. According to Israeli officials, the co-pilot attacked Captain Machchhar in the cockpit and stabbed him.Though badly injured and bleeding on the cockpit floor, the Mumbai-born pilot reportedly managed to trigger the emergency release and open the cockpit door. This let cabin crew and passengers rush in and overpower the attacker. Two off-duty flydubai pilots travelling as passengers then landed the aircraft safely.Captain Machchhar is now being treated at a hospital in Tabuk, where doctors continue to monitor his condition.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Michael B. Jordan: ‘Continue to try to be the best version of yourself,’ a powerful life lesson highlighting a basic requirement for self-growth
articles.summary: Michael B. Jordan’s words offer a simple reminder thatpersonal growth is an ongoing journey.
articles.body: Michael B. Jordan’s words offer a simple reminder thatpersonal growth is an ongoing journey. His message is not about trying to become perfect overnight, but about looking at where you are, learning from your experiences and making a conscious effort to do better with time.Speaking to Extra at the 2026 Critics Choice Awards, Jordan spoke about what he hoped for the year ahead. He said, “I’m looking forward to 2026. Just being better than it was last year." He further mentioned how one should try to continue to be the best version of themselves.Motivational quote of the day by Michael B. Jordan reads: 'Continue to try to be the best version of yourself.'What is the meaning of the quote by Michael B. Jordan?The quote highlights the importance of self-improvement. Jordan’s words suggest that people do not necessarily have to make huge changes to move forward. Even small changes in the way one works, tackles challenges, or builds relationships can make a noticeable difference in one's lifeThe concept of becoming the best version of oneself also makes allowance for the fact that not all days are equal and one cannot always have a productive day at work, be highly efficient or achieve multiple goals. By continuously trying to improve, even if only by small steps but not necessarily by giant leaps, a person remains committed to making his or her life better than it was.Why is the quote relevant today?The quote is particularly relevant in a time when people are constantly exposed to other people’s achievements and lifestyles. Social media can make it easy to compare careers, appearances, much more.His message offers a more personal way of looking at progress. Rather than competing with someone else’s journey, people can focus on their own growth and ask whether they are moving forward from where they were before.Early life of Michael B. articles.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard says Ken Urker overdosed in first comment on partner’s death: ‘Screamed until my throat burns’
articles.summary: The formerly incarcerated personality said she’s “in disbelief” over Urker’s death after he was found dead in his home.
articles.body:
Gypsy Rose Blanchard has commented on the death of ex-fiancé Ken Urker at 34.

Urker was found dead Thursday, his 34th birthday, inside his Louisiana home.

"I'm in disbelief. I can't think," Blanchard said.

The formerly incarcerated Gypsy Rose Blanchard — who was imprisoned over the murder of her mother, Dee Dee Blanchard — has spoken out about the death of her former fiancé Ken Urker , claiming he overdosed and was found in his bed.

After news broke late Thursday, Urker's 34th birthday, that he was found dead in bed in his Louisiana home, Blanchard told Entertainment Weekly 's sister publication PEOPLE that she's "in disbelief" over his death.

"I don't know if it was intentional or not," Blanchard told the outlet, claiming that "he was not in a good state of mind lately."

Blanchard, 35, said she's "screamed until my throat burns" over Urker's death.

"Ken was an amazing father and a man who was deeply loved. He will forever be my soulmate and my red string, a connection that time, distance, and even death can never erase," Blanchard explained, referencing the pair's daughter, Aurora, who was born in December 2024.

Blanchard added that Urker experienced "an unimaginable level of public scrutiny and relentless cyberbullying across social media platforms, including TikTok and Reddit," and that she felt "the cruelty directed toward him was something no human being should have to endure."

"I believe the tremendous weight of that scrutiny and harassment had a profound impact on him, and I hope his passing serves as a reminder that there is a real person behind every screen, every headline, and every comment," she said.

TMZ first reported news of Urker's death. Police in Lafourche, La., told the outlet they "responded to a residence in Raceland today after receiving a call at 6:15 p.m. Kenan Urker, 34, was found dead upon arrival. At this time, we are continuing the death investigation."

The 2015 murder of Blanchard's mother also involved her then-boyfriend, Nicholas Godejohn, who's currently serving a life sentence. The events leading up to the murder — including Dee Dee's Munchausen syndrome by proxy — were highly publicized in the media and in various documentaries, as well as the 2019 Hulu limited series The Act starring Patricia Arquette and Joey King as the mother-daughter pair.

articles.title: Paramount’s Warner Bros. megamerger will just be called Skydance
articles.summary: David Ellison doesn’t want a ‘new corporate identity’ to overshadow Warner Bros. and Paramount’s brands.
articles.body: Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison has announced that the company will just be called Skydance when it completes its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery next week. In a post on X, Ellison writes that “we wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. — and all our extraordinary brands — to remain in the spotlight.” Earlier this week, a judge approved the settlement Paramount reached with California and 11 other states that sued over the planned acquisition, clearing the last major hurdle blocking the deal. Under the deal, Paramount must release a minimum number of theatrical films over the next five years, starting with 30 annually in years one and two. Ahead of the close, Paramount has also appointed Ynon Kreiz, the former chairman and CEO of Mattel, as the co-CEO of the soon-to-be even bigger company. The deal is expected to close on October 6th. Here’s Ellison’s full announcement: > What once was the peak, is now just the beginning. > Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren’t rewriting history — we’re equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling. > We chose this name for a few important reasons. First and foremost, as we bring Paramount and Warner Bros. together, we wanted to preserve what has made each of these studios iconic. Both have distinct identities, extraordinary legacies and brands that have resonated with audiences for generations. We never wanted a new corporate identity to diminish, alter or overshadow either one. Instead, we wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. — and all our extraordinary brands — to remain in the spotlight. > We have big goals for Skydance, and we intend to pursue them with passion, imagination and a willingness to take smart risks. At the same time, we will honor what makes Paramount and Warner Bros. special — giving both studios the opportunity to grow, tell more great stories and bring those stories to even broader audiences around the world, powered by the scale and capabilities of Skydance. > I couldn’t be more excited about what we’re going to build together.

articles.title: Gordon Ramsay admits real reason he was crying while walking daughter down the aisle
articles.summary: Gordon Ramsay reveals feeling "second best" after walking Holly Ramsay down the aisle and jokes about what really made him cry at the wedding.
articles.body: Gordon Ramsay opened up about the bittersweet experience of giving away his daughter, Holly Ramsay, at her wedding. Holly, 26, married Olympic swimmer Adam Peaty, 31, in December 2025 after the couple announced their engagement in 2024. The 59-year-old celebrity chef shares Holly, her twin brother Jack, daughters Megan, 28, and Matilda, 24, and sons Oscar, 7, and Jesse, 2, with his wife, Tana Ramsay, 52, whom he married in 1996. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, Ramsay, who is starring in season two of Apple TV's "Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars," reflected on the close bonds that he shares with his three daughters and explained why he was left feeling "second best" after he walked Holly down the aisle. GORDON RAMSAY SAYS ‘THE MOST IMPORTANT THING’ HE TAUGHT HIS SIX KIDS HAD NOTHING TO DO WITH COOKING "You grow up with these gorgeous girls and you teach them. I said to them, from an early age, they must have been 7 or 8 years of age, ‘The earlier you tell me, the more I can f---ing do," he recalled. "They ignore you for two or three years," Ramsay continued. "But when they get to 11 or 12, ‘Hey daddy, you know what he said to me? The earlier you told me, the more you can do, I have a problem. Can I talk to you about it?’" KELLY RIPA, MARK CONSUELOS SHARE BLUNT ADVICE FOR COUPLES PLANNING A BIG WEDDING "Bang, then we're in,'" he added with a smile. "Then you're like that, you're sort of the BFF, right? Then you're a cool f---ing dad, then you're perfect. But when you walk them down the aisle, and you're minutes away from not being the number one guy in their life, and you're handing them over, man, that hits. That absolutely hits." "So you have to understand that that relationship with your daughter is borrowed time before there's another man in their lives. Another partner in their life, that you become second best." WATCH: GORDON RAMSAY ADMITS REAL REASON HE WAS CRYING WHILE WALKING DAUGHTER DOWN THE AISLE The "Hell's Kitchen" star noted that as a father of six, he will have to experience those moments multiple times in the future. "I have ages to go through all that s---," he said. "Three boys and three girls." Ramsay, who is famous for his fiery temper and tough demeanor in the kitchen, admitted to becoming emotional at Holly's wedding but joked that it was not for the reason that most people would expect. "I was like a sack of f---ing custard walking down that bloody — that line — into that church. 60 meters!" he recalled. "And I was looking at all these flowers overlooking the pews and thinking, ‘S---, this is expensive!' Everyone thought I was crying because I was giving her away. I was more crying with the f---ing cost of the flower bill, and where are they going tomorrow? We're paying all this money for 90 minutes, these flowers." DANA PERINO: FIVE IMPORTANT LESSONS FROM MY FATHER FOR EVERY PROUD GIRL DAD Ramsay quipped that his tears dried up once he realized that the flowers could be repurposed for a good cause. "We got the flowers donated to the local hospital and that stopped me crying," he said. "And then I handed her over, and I celebrated like no tomorrow, because that daughter was expensive." CLINT BLACK AND LISA HARTMAN BLACK'S ONE RULE THAT HAS KEPT THEIR MARRIAGE STRONG FOR NEARLY 35 YEARS Holly and Peaty's wedding took place on Dec. 27, 2025, at The Abbey Church of Saint Peter and Saint Paul in Bath, England. During a January interview with People, Ramsay admitted that he was nervous about giving his father-of-the-bride speech. "It's tough, honestly — I mean, being a dad with three daughters, you dream of that moment. That moment arrives, and you're just like a hot mess," he told the outlet. "The speech was perfect. It went well. You got to find that sort of — you've got to be warm, emotional ... It was just a tough gig." Tilly told People that Ramsay spent about an hour rehearsing his speech in front of her on Christmas Eve. She said that while Ramsay pored over every word, ultimately "no tweaks were needed." "It was perfect," Tilly said. "It made everybody cry." ‘CHARLIE’S ANGELS’ STAR JACLYN SMITH LIVED APART FROM HER HUSBAND FOR 17 YEARS DURING THEIR 35-YEAR LOVE STORY Holly wore three different dresses on her wedding day, including her mother's gown from her 1996 nuptials with Ramsay. The TV personality told People that seeing Holly in Tana's wedding dress came as "a bit of a shock." While speaking with British Vogue in January, Holly noted that wearing the gown during her father-daughter dance with Ramsay was especially meaningful because "the last time Dad saw this dress was when he danced with my mom at their wedding." At the time, Holly told the outlet that Ramsay became emotional whenever she discussed the wedding leading up to her big day. "Dad cries every time I talk about the wedding," she said. "The other day I was asking him which car he and I would take to the church, and he welled up immediately." Though Holly is the first of Ramsay's six children to walk down the aisle, he will soon have to give another daughter away. In an August appearance on "Live with Kelly and Mark," he revealed that Megan was engaged. During his interview with Fox News Digital, Ramsay noted that he needed to start preparing for Megan's nuptials. "I've got to get my dance act together, especially with another wedding coming up next year," he said. "Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars," which is executive produced by Ramsay, made its debut on Apple TV in October 2025. Hosted by food expert Jesse Burgess, the documentary series follows chefs around the world as they pursue Michelin stars while balancing the personal and professional sacrifices required to achieve culinary excellence. While speaking with Fox News Digital, Ramsay admitted that his own pursuit of perfection in the kitchen had come at a cost. Looking back, the "MasterChef" star reflected on the biggest sacrifice that he made while building his restaurant empire. "Time," he said. "You become one of the most, sort of, you know, selfish individuals because you need to focus. And so I'd say the sacrifice was less time with the family straight off the bat." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "There's a lot of situations in ‘Knife Edge,' you'll see families working together. That's actually harder," he continued. "My wife and I decided that 'Look, the time we have is little, but it'd be quality.' It won't be great, long time, but it would be quality. And then my kids appreciate the time they had with me." "They didn't see me seven nights a week," Ramsay said. "I didn't do the school runs. I wasn't doing the dinners and the goodbyes and the plays and all the nativities. I couldn't do that. And so, don't forget when all your mates are out celebrating, you're working because they're either eating at the restaurants or out going to another restaurant." "So yeah, I'd say time, the biggest, the most expensive ingredient in the world, time," he added. "And you have to sacrifice that time." Ramsay, whose restaurants currently hold nine Michelin stars worldwide, has earned a total of 17 Michelin stars over the course of his career. His flagship Restaurant Gordon Ramsay in London has held the maximum three Michelin stars continuously since 2001. Ramsay's portfolio gained a ninth star earlier this year when Restaurant Gordon Ramsay High in London's Bishopsgate area earned its first Michelin star in the 2026 Michelin Guide. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE According to the official synopsis, season two of "Knife Edge" "follows 16 restaurants at pivotal moments in their journeys: A chef and his family risk everything to put a tiny island on Michelin’s map. Two generations of a legendary culinary family pursue recognition on their own terms. Two chefs voluntarily give up their Star when they open a new restaurant and have just 52 days to win it back." "One sandwich shop transforms into a fine-dining restaurant each night, while a young couple seeks to put Filipino cuisine at the center of one of America’s most competitive dining scenes. Their circumstances could hardly be more different, yet each faces the same uncertainty: when Michelin makes its decision, will everything they have strived for be enough?" Ramsay noted that "Knife Edge" pulls back the curtain on the countless hours of preparation and discipline that diners rarely see before a meal reaches the table. "Finally, now we have a show on Apple that really unfolds that unscripted drama and follows the highs and lows, the emotions, the pressures that these restaurants are under — especially today," he said. The celebrity chef told Fox News Digital that he hopes the show gives viewers a new appreciation for the commitment behind every Michelin-starred meal. "I'd love the audience to take away from ‘Knife Edge' season 2 the understanding of pursuit for perfection and the price they pay is extraordinary," Ramsay said. "And then to understand properly, the commitment to perfection. You go to games and live sports, and you see that energy and the excitement and the touchdowns and the medals and the ceremony. It's the exact same for a restaurant. That you don't even see." articles.title: Sanjeev Kumar did C-grade films as he was broke, lent Rs 96 lakhs to his friends, 5-6 lakhs to Shatrughan Sinha: 'He suffered two heart attacks when he met Sulakshana Pandit'
articles.summary: Sanjeev Kumar remains one of Hindi cinema’s most respected actors, remembered for his performances in films such as ‘Sholay’, ‘Aandhi’, ‘Trishul’,
articles.body: Sanjeev Kumar remains one of Hindi cinema’s most respected actors, remembered for his performances in films such as ‘Sholay’, ‘Aandhi’, ‘Trishul’, ‘Koshish’ and ‘Mausam’. However, before achieving stardom, the actor went through a difficult financial phase and reportedly took up whatever work came his way. Journalist Hanif Zaveri recently recalled that Sanjeev was so financially strained during the early years of his career that he even worked in C-grade films to support his family.In a conversation on the Meri Saheli Podcast’s YouTube channel, Zaveri spoke about Sanjeev’s struggling years, when he was trying to establish himself in the film industry while his family was also dealing with financial difficulties. According to him, the actor owned just two sets of clothes at the time, while his mother was trying to cope with his father’s failing business."He didn't know that the films he was doing were C-grade. He was quite broke, so he was doing whatever work he could get," recalled Hanif Zaveri.Despite experiencing financial hardships himself, Sanjeev was known for being generous towards those around him. Zaveri claimed that the actor lent Rs 96 lakh to several friends over the years, but never received the money back. He also recalled instances of Sanjeev paying for his driver’s wedding and gifting a car to a friend."He gave Rs 96 lakh away as loans to his friends, who never paid him back. He paid for his driver's wedding. He gifted a car to one of his friends. When Sanjeev made his will, he kept Rs 2 lakh aside for his driver's son's education. People who are miserly don't do this. He was simply against unnecessary expenditure," added Zaveri.Zaveri further recalled how Sanjeev helped fellow actors and filmmakers without expecting anything in return. He said the actor gave money to Shatrughan Sinha when he needed it, even though Sinha had not asked him for financial help. He also claimed that Sanjeev gave money to filmmaker Boney Kapoor without any formal paperwork."When Shatrughan Sinha needed money, Sanjeev Kumar gave it to him even though Shatrughan hadn't asked for it. Boney Kapoor needed money too, so he gave it to him as well, without any documentation or formalities. After Sanjeev died, Boney returned the money to his family. Even the family didn't know he had given that money," he said.The journalist also spoke about the friendship between Sanjeev Kumar and Shatrughan Sinha. He recalled how Sanjeev supported Sinha during the early stages of his career after the latter returned from the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII)."They shared a deep friendship. When Sanjeev got to know that Shatrughan needed money, he was the first person to help out. He gave around Rs 5-7 lakh," added the journalist.While Sanjeev eventually went on to work with some of the biggest filmmakers in the industry and establish himself as a celebrated actor, his personal life remained complicated. Zaveri spoke about his relationships with Hema Malini and Nutan before discussing his later relationship with actor-singer Sulakshana Pandit.According to Zaveri, Sanjeev chose not to marry Sulakshana because he was convinced that he would have a short life. He had already suffered two heart attacks by the time they met and reportedly believed that he would not live beyond the age of 50 because several men in his family had died young."He had already suffered two heart attacks by the time he met Sulakshana Pandit. He did not want to marry anyone. He believed that he had a short life, and he felt this way because all the men in his family had died before the age of 50. He believed that he too would die before turning 50, so he did not want to get married and spoil someone else's life. That was the only reason why he did not marry her," said Hanif.Sanjeev Kumar passed away on November 6, 1985, at the age of 47. Interestingly, Sulakshana Pandit died on the same date in 2025.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Ben Affleck rejects 'propaganda' opposing AI, insists emerging technology will help filmmakers
articles.summary: Ben Affleck slammed AI "propaganda" while speaking at Bloomberg Screentime 2026, saying he used the technology for "lots of things" for his new film.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — Ben Affleck is fed up with what he calls "propaganda" against artificial intelligence as he has become one of Hollywood's most vocal proponents of the emerging technology. Affleck made headlines in July when it was announced that Netflix paid him a whopping $587 million for his AI startup InterPositive, a venture virtually no one in the industry knew he had been working on. Appearing Wednesday at the Bloomberg Screentime summit, Affleck was asked about the "cynical take" critics had over the deal, which claimed Netflix bought his company so it can do "despicable things" with AI with a reputable filmmaker attached to "provide cover." "Well, that's a very cynical view indeed," Affleck reacted to the question. NETFLIX CHIEF ADMITS TRUMP IS HELPING SHOWBIZ INDUSTRY AS FEDERAL TAX CREDIT BILL AIMS TO FUEL HOLLYWOOD JOBS The Oscar-winning writer and producer insisted Netflix isn't in a position to do "despicable things" and alienate artists because "they need to be in business with people," describing the streamer as being "super judicious" when it comes to his various projects. "I'm sitting down with directors going, 'Look, man, you can just, you can change the background here, you can do this, you can do that.' And what I find is that filmmakers and people — once they sit with it and have a sense of control and a sense of understanding what's happening, and it moves from this nebulous abstract terrifying alien, you know, 'It's gonna to kill us all like we're paper clips…' all this propaganda," Affleck said. "And they actually see what it is — it's another form of computing that does tools and is a technological advancement that's really in keeping with a long-standing series of technological improvements we've made in the film and television business." CONAN O'BRIEN COMPARES DECLINING LATE-NIGHT TV LANDSCAPE TO DETROIT "It's like the switch. They go, 'Oh great, wonderful.' And it's being used on films now where they're the same number of people. In fact, more people, technically, are being employed. And I think it's — they have been absolutely, in my view, true to their word of we want to make what we're doing better. We're not trying to just, you know, slash cost or do heinous things," he continued. The "Argo" director revealed he used AI for "lots of things" in his forthcoming Netflix film "Animals," but refrained from pointing to specific examples of it, comparing it to a magician spoiling their tricks. CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS When asked what parts of the industry he thought would be most affected by AI, Affleck dismissed concerns about an industry takeover by the technology. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "When I worry about AI, I worry about like my kids in school. I worry about 30% rise in, you know, the number of As given out at colleges over the last three years. I worry about learned helplessness. I worry about responsible use. I don't worry about Skynet and I don't think that it's going to take over this business in any meaningful way. I think it's going to be additive," Affleck said, referencing the fictional AI system in the "Terminator" movies. "But I think someone has to actually step in and do it in a way where it is that you can't just bury your head in the sand. It needs to be incorporated. Like a lot of technologies, it requires getting comfortable and getting familiar with. And then immediately it's knowable. You see all the ways in which it doesn't work, all the failures. The sort of dumb nature of it in a lot of ways, and it becomes a knowable thing," he added.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Tom Selleck: ‘You must develop an appetite for failure because the only way you can risk being good in the acting business is to stick your neck out to risk failing,’ a powerful life lesson highlighting the importance of challenges and setbacks
articles.summary: Discover Tom Selleck's powerful quote on the importance of embracing failure for success in acting and other creative careers. Learn how setbacks pave the way to growth and achievement.
articles.body: It has often been noticed that unsuccessful auditions and missed opportunities stay hidden behind the shine of big achievements. It is important to acknowledge that every big win comes after a series of failures. Tom Selleck has never treated those setbacks as something to be ashamed of. For the veteran actor, failure has been part of learning what works, taking chances and staying in the business long enough to find the right opportunity.Today’s quote of the day by Tom Selleck reads: “You must develop an appetite for failure because the only way you can risk being good in the acting business is to stick your neck out to risk failing.”What does the quote by Tom Selleck mean?Selleck shared this thought during a 2012 phone interview with Conversation. He was discussing what he tells young people who are interested in becoming actors. His advice was straightforward: if someone wants to become genuinely good at the craft, they cannot spend all their time trying to avoid failure.The phrase “appetite for failure” does not mean that failure itself should be the goal. Instead, Selleck was talking about becoming comfortable with the possibility of getting things wrong. Acting requires auditions, difficult roles and choices that may not work. If an actor becomes too worried about looking bad or making a mistake, they may never take the kind of chances that help them improve.For Selleck, taking that risk was closely connected to learning. In the same interview, he explained that failure teaches people something that success sometimes cannot. His point is especially relevant to creative careers, where there is rarely a guaranteed path from effort to recognition.Why does Tom Selleck’s message still matter today?Selleck’s words can apply well beyond acting. Students, writers, entrepreneurs, artists and professionals often hesitate to try something because they are worried about getting it wrong. That fear can become stronger when success appears so visible online. People see finished projects, promotions, awards and achievements, but they rarely see every unsuccessful attempt that came before them. Selleck’s message asks people to look at the process differently.Taking a risk does not guarantee success, but avoiding every risk can also limit what a person learns. A failed interview can reveal what needs improvement. A rejected idea can lead to a better one. Even an unsuccessful project can show someone what they do not want to pursue.Tom Selleck’s early lifeTom Selleck was born on January 29, 1945, in Detroit, Michigan, and his family later moved to Los Angeles. He attended the University of Southern California on a basketball scholarship and studied business while also working as a model. At first, becoming a big Hollywood actor wasn’t really the plan for Selleck.Selleck eventually began pursuing acting more seriously. He signed with 20th Century Fox in the late 1960s and spent years taking small roles, commercials and television appearances. The work was not always steady, and several television pilots he appeared in failed to become series.Tom Selleck’s rise to fameSelleck finally got his big break in 1980 with Magnum, P.I. He played the role of a private investigator, Thomas Magnum. Tom Selleck was 35 at that point, after years of smaller jobs and unsuccessful projects. The role turned him into a major television star and earned him both an Emmy and a Golden Globe. His career later expanded into films, television dramas, and comedy, with roles in 'Three Men and a Baby', 'Friends,' 'Jesse Stone,' and 'Blue Bloods'.Even after becoming established, Selleck continued speaking about the uncertainty inherent in an acting career.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Anne Hathaway Says She’s ‘Chilled Out’ About Fame After Blockbuster Year: ‘I Have Changed’
articles.summary: Anne Hathaway’s ‘Verity,’ which also stars Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett, is in theaters now
articles.body:
Anne Hathaway reflected on navigating fame and learning not to take high-pressure moments so personally

Verity is her fifth film release of 2026 and stars Dakota Johnson and Josh Hartnett

Two of Hathaway's 2026 films rank among the year's top 10 domestic box office releases

Anne Hathaway is explaining how she's having a little more fun with her career these days.

Hathaway, 43, appeared on CBS Mornings on Friday, Oct. 2, for an interview with Gayle King about her new movie Verity , the last of five movies the Academy Award winner has appeared in during 2026.

During the interview, King, 71, noted that Hathaway — who is pregnant and expecting her third baby with husband Adam Shulman and has been in the public eye throughout much of this year — appears to be embracing her success after navigating an at-times rocky relationship with fame in the past.

"Well, thank you for saying that and thank you for highlighting all those wonderful things. But I do think I have changed," Hathaway said. "I do think when I show up to something like this — you know, the joke you made about 'don't freeze,' 'cause that can happen. I know this is a big deal, but it's not everything, no offense. And so if I freeze on set, it's not the end of the world. There's a lot of people around who are there. And maybe they're actually hoping that the best thing happens. So I think that I've chilled out, which I think was necessary. And I think I'm more open to the fun of it."

"And to not take it all so personally," King added.

"It's actually just about the feeling and the connection that you have with other people," Hathaway responded. "And I wish that I figured that out earlier in my life, but I'm so grateful that I did at all."

Verity marks the final release in Hathaway's impressive five-film run in 2026 , following Mother Mary , The Devil Wears Prada 2 , The Odyssey and The End of Oak Street .

In the new movie, adapted from author Colleen Hoover's novel of the same name, Hathaway portrays Verity Crawford, a successful and reclusive author. The movie follows another writer, Lowen ( Dakota Johnson ), who is hired by Verity's husband, Jeremy ( Josh Hartnett ), to finish a series of books Verity had begun writing before suffering an accident. But Lowen's experience with the couple takes a chilling turn when she discovers a separate, unfinished manuscript written by Verity.

On CBS Mornings , King asked Hathaway whether she worried about people seeing "a lot of [her]" when she realized all five movies would be released within one calendar year.

"A little bit, of course. I mean, it's a lot and you want to be able to show up fully for each film," Hathaway responded. "And that's asking a lot of people to look at you for a long period of time. But then I thought to myself, 'What if it goes better than you'd imagine?'"

Two of Hathaway's releases this year — The Odyssey and The Devil Wears Prada 2 — currently rank among the 10 highest-grossing movies of 2026 at the domestic box office . articles.title: Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery to become Skydance
articles.summary: The roughly $110 billion deal is expected to close October 6.
articles.body:
Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will operate as Skydance once their merger closes, Paramount CEO David Ellison announced Friday . Skydance is the name of Ellison’s original film production company.

The roughly $110 billion deal is expected to close October 6. It will combine two major Hollywood studios, Paramount+ and HBO Max, and networks including CBS, CNN, MTV, TBS, Comedy Central, and Food Network. Skydance will also control franchises such as “The Lord of the Rings,” “Game of Thrones,” the DC Universe, and “Yellowstone.”

The merger followed a drawn-out corporate battle. Netflix had agreed to acquire Warner Bros.’ streaming and studio businesses before the broader Paramount deal moved forward. Twelve states challenged the deal, arguing it could reduce competition and harm consumers and workers, but a judge approved a settlement with the state attorneys general this week.

Ellison said the Paramount and Warner Bros. brands will remain central. “We never wanted a new corporate identity to diminish, alter or overshadow either one,” he wrote on X. The new name, he said, gives the company “an identity of its own” while letting both studios “remain in the spotlight.”

articles.title: In 1972, Elton John bought his first home and named it Hercules; inside the Rocket Man’s extraordinary world of art, cars and maximalist interiors
articles.summary: Elton John has spent more than six decades creating a visual identity that is almost as recognisable as his music.
articles.body: Elton John has spent more than six decades creating a visual identity that is almost as recognisable as his music. From extravagant stage costumes and towering platform shoes to colourful glasses and glittering accessories, the singer has rarely shied away from excess. His homes have reflected that same fascination with colour, art and unusual objects, although his approach to interiors has changed considerably over the years.One of the earliest glimpses of John at home dates back to 1972, when he bought his first property in Virginia Water, Surrey. He called the three-bedroom house Hercules, taking the name from the middle name he had recently adopted after legally changing his name from Reginald Kenneth Dwight to Elton Hercules John. The property also inspired the title of “Hercules,” a song from his 1972 album Honky Château.Photographs from the period show the young musician outside the house with a collection of cars, offering a glimpse into his life during a period when his career was rapidly taking off. Inside, his taste was already unmistakable. His walls were decorated with Art Nouveau posters, while his growing collection of books, records and decorative objects began turning the property into a reflection of his interests.Woodside became the heart of his English lifeIn 1974, John purchased Woodside, a large estate near Windsor in Berkshire. The Queen Anne-influenced country house eventually became his longest-running residence in England and was transformed several times over the years.His relationship with the property changed dramatically as his collection grew. By the late 1980s, Woodside was packed with possessions accumulated during John’s years as an international superstar. Vintage pinball machines, costumes, lamps, memorabilia and other collectibles had filled the rooms to such an extent that the house had become difficult to navigate.According to Architectural Digest, John later described the earlier version of Woodside as being closer to an “Aladdin’s cave” than a conventional home. Following his rehabilitation in 1990, he wanted his surroundings to feel calmer and more like a traditional English country house. Designers Adrian Cooper-Grigg and Andrew Protheroe were brought in to completely rethink the interiors.His maximalism became more carefully curatedThe redesign did not mean that John abandoned his love for dramatic interiors. Instead, his collections were incorporated into rooms that had a more cohesive and traditional character.The estate features classic English furnishings, artwork, a library and extensive gardens. One of its more unusual spaces is the library, which was created from what had previously been a squash court. Another distinctive part of the property is the restored 18th-century orangery, which John turned into a peaceful retreat filled with antiques and artwork.His approach to decorating also allowed seemingly unrelated objects to exist together. Paintings, antique furniture, porcelain, photographs and decorative pieces could share the same space, creating interiors that feel personal rather than tied to one particular design trend.His love for collecting went far beyond furnitureFor John, collecting has never been limited to decorating a room. Over the years, he has accumulated major collections spanning photography, contemporary art, glass, furniture, fashion and memorabilia.Photography became one of his most important passions, particularly after he became sober. Christie’s says John and his husband David Furnish built one of the world’s largest private photography collections, with works by celebrated photographers including Irving Penn, Herb Ritts and other major names.The collection has also been exhibited publicly. John’s photographs were shown at the High Museum of Art in Atlanta in 2000 and later at Tate Modern in London. In 2024, more than 300 photographs from the collection were displayed at London’s Victoria and Albert Museum as part of Fragile Beauty: Photographs from the Sir Elton John and David Furnish Collection.Atlanta became another canvas for his collectionsJohn’s Atlanta home became particularly important to his life and collecting habits. He purchased a duplex apartment at Park Place on Peachtree Road in 1991, eventually combining several units into a much larger residence.Over the following three decades, the property evolved into an enormous private gallery. Christie’s records that the combined residence eventually covered more than 13,500 square feet and housed photographs, contemporary art, furniture, fashion and personal objects.The home was also closely linked to John’s creative life. During his years in Atlanta, he worked on music for projects including Billy Elliot and Aida, while the city itself became an important part of his personal and professional story.The Atlanta collection eventually went under the hammerAfter John retired from touring, the Atlanta chapter came to an end. In 2024, Christie’s presented The Collection of Sir Elton John: Goodbye Peachtree Road, a series of auctions featuring more than 900 objects from his former residence.The sale included clothing, photographs, artwork, furniture, memorabilia and some of the objects most closely associated with his flamboyant public image. The complete series realised $20,537,842, with photography accounting for approximately one-third of the lots.Among the items offered were his stagewear, platform boots, sunglasses, furniture and a 1990 Bentley Continental convertible. The auction provided collectors with an unusually detailed look at the objects that had surrounded John during more than three decades in Atlanta.A home that mirrors an extraordinary careerThe photographs of Elton John at home tell a story that goes beyond celebrity property. They show how his private surroundings evolved alongside his career and personal life.The young musician who filled Hercules with records, posters and collections eventually became an established collector with homes containing significant works of art and photography. His interiors became more sophisticated, but the instinct to surround himself with things he loved never disappeared.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Missouri man adopted as baby learns biological father is rock star Michael McDonald
articles.summary: When Michael Goessling, 59, heard his biological father’s voice for the first time last year, he swore he recognized it and asked: “Are you Michael McDonald?”
articles.body: When Michael Goessling, 59, heard his biological father’s voice for the first time last year, he swore he recognized it. “I just said: ‘What a voice that guy has!’... it just sounded so familiar, but I couldn’t place it.” When they spoke over the phone that night, it clicked. “Finally, I just said: ‘Are you Michael McDonald?’” Goessling recalled. “And he chuckled and he said, ‘Yeah, I’m afraid so.’” McDonald, a five-time Grammy winner who is lead vocalist of the Doobie Brothers and a successful solo artist, had a child in Missouri with his middle school sweetheart and neighbor when they were 14-years-old, Goessling told NBC News on Friday. The pair gave up the baby in a closed adoption to Goessling’s parents, who lived roughly 20 minutes away in a suburb of St. Louis, and went their separate ways, Goessling said. Nearly 58 years later, they reached out to their son. In May, Goessling said he received a letter in the mail from his biological parents asking to make contact. The 59-year-old said they tracked him down after one of Goessling’s half-brother’s found him through a 23andMe DNA test. Goessling said he spoke with his biological mother that night and suggested that they get lunch that Friday — a date which had sentimental value. “She became very emotional and said, ‘Your birthday.’ And I said ‘Yes, you’ve waited long enough. I’ve waited long enough. Let’s meet on my birthday, 58 years to the day,’” he said. The pair met that Friday, and Goessling got a voice memo from his biological father that night. Goessling and McDonald spoke over the phone for the first time the following day. Going into the call, Goessling said he knew only his father’s first name. “I said to Mike, ‘So hey, tell me, what do you do?’ And he said, ‘Well, I’m a musician.’ And I said, ‘That is awesome. I love music. I’ve always been a music nut,’” Goessling said. Goessling said his biological father told him he had a show in St. Louis on Sept. 4, 2025. “I was surprised by that statement, having done the math and knowing how old he was,” Goessling said. “Being a touring musician was not what I was expecting.” He said he figured McDonald was part of some sort of small touring orchestra, until McDonald revealed in passing that he was performing at the Hollywood Casino Amphitheater. When Goessling Googled who was playing at the music hall on the date and saw it was the Doobie Brothers, he pieced his father’s identity together. “There are still days I wake up, and my first thought is I am coming out of the craziest dream, and it’s been a year and a half,” Goessling said. “I’m still trying to get my head around all of it.” Goessling has listened to the Doobie Brothers since he was a little boy and remembers when McDonald replaced lead singer and guitarist Tom Johnston in 1975, he said. He said he was 8- or 9-years-old when the switch occurred, and got into an argument with other children about whether or not a song they were listening to was actually one of the band’s. “They told me, ‘No, they got a new singer. It’s Michael McDonald.’ And I was like, ‘Well, this is awesome,’” he said. “And I was just a fan from the get go.” Goessling said he’s seen the Doobie Brothers in concert twice before learning McDonald was his biological father. His adopted family was supportive of his reunification with his biological parents, Goessling said. For the first time, Goessling’s entire family got together the evening before McDonald’s concert in St. Louis, which he described as “one of the greatest events of my life.” Goessling said that he later learned his biological parents had made several attempts to reach him in his life with similar letters, but he did not receive them. He said that although his biological parents both dated other people and had other children, they remained good friends over the years. “I just wanted to thank them for the choices they made on my behalf and for giving me a shot in this world, and how grateful I was for that,” he said. “They were always heroes in my story.”

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE: Michael McDonald’s long-lost son reveals stunning moment he discovered famous father after 58 years
articles.summary: A St. Louis man adopted through Catholic Charities nearly 60 years ago learned his biological father is Doobie Brothers singer Michael McDonald.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE: Michael Goessling always knew he was adopted. But what he did not know for nearly 58 years was that his biological father had one of the most recognizable and beloved voices in American music. The St. Louis man learned recently that his father is five-time Grammy winner and Doobie Brothers singer Michael McDonald, a musician Goessling had admired since childhood and had unknowingly paid to see perform twice as a young man. But even after receiving the letter that began it all, meeting his biological mother and learning his biological father was a mysterious musician named "Mike," Goessling still had no idea who was waiting on the other end of the phone. RITA WILSON LEARNED ABOUT FATHER’S TRAGIC PAST, SECRET FAMILY IN BULGARIA ON TV SHOW The answer finally came during their first conversation, when "Mike" mentioned he was touring and would be stopping in St. Louis on Sept. 4 at a venue he believed was called "Hollywood." Goessling thought of the Hollywood Casino Amphitheater and, puzzled that his biological father was apparently still a touring musician at his age, began searching the venue's concert schedule as the two men spoke. The Doobie Brothers were playing in concert Sept. 4. Suddenly, the pieces began falling into place: "Mike." Musician. That unmistakable voice. "Are you Michael McDonald?" Goessling finally asked. McDonald chuckled. "Yep, afraid so." "Oh my gosh, this is getting crazier by the second," Goessling recalled saying. "I can't even, I can't get my head around this. This is too much." "I know," McDonald replied. "Take a minute." "I thought I was being punked for a second," Goessling told Fox News Digital. "It's like, 'No, this can't be real. This is impossible. What is going on here?'" More than a year later, he said the discovery can still feel unreal. NEW CALIFORNIA LAW EXPANDS DNA TOOLS FOR MISSING PERSONS INVESTIGATIONS "I still wake up sometimes and my first thought is, ‘Oh my gosh, that was a crazy dream,’ only to realize that here we are." The extraordinary phone call came just days after a letter ended a mystery stretching back to Goessling's birth. On May 6, 2025, an attorney representing his biological mother contacted Goessling to explain that she believed he was the son she had placed for adoption through Catholic Charities nearly 58 years earlier. Goessling had always known he was adopted, but the adoption was closed. He knew nothing about his biological parents, and they knew virtually nothing about the life he had gone on to live. His biological mother, he learned, had spent roughly 30 to 35 years searching for him. Both biological parents hoped he might be willing to communicate, Goessling recalled, but above all, they wanted to know that he was well. "It was a wonderful surprise but quite a shock," he said. "It felt like a tsunami hit me." Goessling called his biological mother that evening. Although he had never actively searched for his biological parents, he had long hoped he might someday have the opportunity to thank them. "I just want you to hear from me that I got nothing but love for you," he recalled telling her. "This is such an amazing gift, that I get to thank you personally. … They were always heroes in my story," he said. CUT OFF BY YOUR ADULT CHILD? PSYCHOLOGY RESEARCHER REVEALS WHAT PARENTS SHOULD DO NEXT Their first conversation lasted about 90 minutes. Goessling eventually proposed meeting for lunch that Friday, prompting his biological mother to remind him that Friday was his birthday. "Yeah, yeah. You've waited long enough. I think I've waited enough," he recalled replying. "Let's meet on my birthday, 58 years to the day." After a three-hour lunch and nearly six decades apart, Goessling learned there was someone else anxious to speak with him. His biological father had deliberately remained in the background so mother and son could have their reunion first. "He really wanted the mother-son thing to happen first, which is just true to his character," Goessling said. "He thought that was very important, and he wanted to take a back seat so that could happen." Before father and son connected, McDonald left Goessling a voicemail. That unmistakable voice immediately struck him. "Whoa, what a voice," Goessling recalled telling his biological mother. "Yeah, he gets that a lot," she replied with a chuckle. The voice seemed strangely familiar, but Goessling still didn't make the connection. When the two men finally spoke, he began by telling McDonald what he had already told his biological mother. "Thank you for giving me a shot in this world," Goessling recalled saying. "I've had a charmed life. And it all started with you guys." Then he asked what his biological father did for a living. "I'm a musician," McDonald told him. Goessling, a lifelong music obsessive who once worked in the music business, thought that was terrific. It wasn't until the conversation turned to McDonald's upcoming tour stop that he finally put it together. The revelation contained another coincidence almost too remarkable to invent; Goessling was already a huge fan. The Doobie Brothers had been among his favorite bands since childhood, alongside The Who and Journey. He vividly remembers first hearing "Takin' It to the Streets" after McDonald joined the group and insisting to the person playing it that there had been some mistake. "I know the Doobie Brothers and that is not the Doobie Brothers," Goessling remembered declaring as a child. He soon learned about the band's new singer and became a McDonald fan, too. He remained one. In fact, Goessling had already watched his biological father perform in concert twice, once in the 1980s, and again in the early 1990s, without ever imagining that the man onstage was the father whose identity he did not know. When Fox News Digital pointed out that meant he had actually paid twice to see his own father perform, Goessling laughed. "I should get reimbursed for that." There were other clues hiding in plain sight. After Goessling grew out his hair and white beard during the COVID-19 pandemic, people began telling him they liked the "Michael McDonald thing" he had going on. "Little did I know, five years later that that would resonate even so true," he said. After the families met, the similarities became even harder to miss. During a visit with McDonald, Goessling said McDonald's wife, Amy, and his newfound half-sister would watch him do or say something and suddenly burst out laughing. "Your dad does the exact same thing," they would tell him. "They couldn't take their eyes off me," Goessling said. "They're waiting to see what I would do or say next because there was so many just natural similarities." Yet, for Goessling, the remarkable celebrity connection is not the part of his story that matters most. Learning where he came from also meant finally understanding what his biological parents had faced nearly six decades earlier, when they were just two 14-year-old eighth-graders confronting a pregnancy that would change all three of their lives. According to Goessling, the teenagers' initial reaction was that they would marry, raise their baby and rely on their families to help them. Their parents concluded they were simply too young at the time. "They were just far too young to be married and to have a child," Goessling said. Their families ultimately determined that adoption would be best, he said, although relinquishing their son had not been his biological parents' first choice. Nearly six decades later, Goessling sees what happened through the lens of both gratitude and faith. "Mike, I mean, he wasn't Michael McDonald [then]. He was Mike from the neighborhood," he said, imagining how differently life could have been had two 14-year-olds attempted to raise a child together. "I have to believe that it all worked out as it was supposed to because, certainly, when I see us all now together, it's just the greatest joy," Goessling said. "I think this was the plan. And I think it was a beautiful plan." That plan, as Goessling sees it, led him to Paul and Kay Goessling. He grew up in a family of four children. Three were adopted before, against the odds, Kay became pregnant with their youngest daughter, Linda. Goessling describes his childhood as "charmed" and said he could not have chosen better parents himself. "If I could go back and pick two folks, I would pick them and do it all over again," he said. "They were just the most wonderful blessing in my life." His father, Paul, died shortly before Christmas 2024 after a long battle with Parkinson's disease, and Goessling said the two were extremely close. Six months later, another father entered his life. "After losing my father, I get a letter, and Mike pops up," Goessling said. "Another father enters my life, my world." Kay's reaction to the discovery was immediate. When Goessling showed her the letter, he said his mother began crying and declared what had happened "a miracle." She asked whether he had met his biological mother, and he had. "Oh my God, go get her," Goessling recalled Kay saying. "I have to meet her. I've got a million questions. What's she like? I gotta give her a big hug." Goessling said his mother has embraced his biological family from the beginning, and the once-separate branches of his family came together with surprising ease. "Everybody's in love with everybody," he said. Father and son now speak frequently and text "all the time," according to Goessling. And while the identity of his biological father is what thrust his story into the spotlight, Goessling hopes the attention gives him an opportunity to talk about adoption as a blessing. A practicing Catholic who was raised in the faith and adopted through Catholic Charities, Goessling said his parents taught him from childhood to understand his adoption not as evidence that he had been unwanted, but as evidence that he was deeply loved. Even before he was old enough to fully understand what adoption meant, he knew how his parents viewed it. "It was a miracle," he said. "It was the greatest thing. It was a gift from God." Only when Goessling grew old enough to understand where babies came from, he said, did he fully appreciate the significance of the decisions that had been made before his birth. "Obviously, we all know there are choices in this world, and I am so grateful and fortunate for the choices they made on my behalf," he said. "Adoption has been absolutely nothing but a blessing for me. … I celebrate adoption and I always have. It's always been a big part of my life story." Now, nearly six decades later, Goessling has been able to thank the biological parents he once could only imagine, and discovered that they had spent those same decades wondering about him. He hopes the unlikely circumstances that brought attention to his family can help "elevate" the conversation surrounding adoption. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I want this to elevate the narrative, the adoption narrative," he said. "I want that adoption gets celebrated more in this country. If my crazy story can be true, Lord knows anything is possible." And if Michael McDonald is watching? Goessling doesn't need an interview to deliver the message. He said father and son already talk regularly. "I just tell him that I love him, and I tell him thank you for everything," he said. After 58 years, the man who says he never felt deprived of a family has somehow ended up with an even larger one. "My cup overflows," Goessling said.

articles.title: Michael Douglas ADMITS to secret affair with Kathleen Turner during 'Romancing the Stone'; says he lied about romance to 'protect my wife and son'
articles.summary: Michael Douglas is coming clean about a secret affair he had with his co-star, about four decades ago.
articles.body: Michael Douglas is coming clean about a secret affair he had with his co-star, about four decades ago.The veteran Hollywood star, who is set to launch his new memoir, 'One Helluva Ride', revealed that he and Kathleen Turner secretly dated while filming 'Romancing the Stone'. In his new book, he also revealed the reason behind calling off the romance.Michael Douglas admits affair with Kathleen TurnerDouglas, now 82, admitted that he and Turner, now 72, were romantically involved while working together on the 1984 adventure comedy. Reflecting on his first meeting with the actress, Douglas wrote, “Kathleen was smart, funny, and sexy with a deep, sultry voice that became her signature. I instantly liked her, and we were immediately attracted to each other.”The pair’s chemistry became a talking point among fans, but both actors repeatedly denied rumours of a romance brewing under the radar. Acknowledging the rumours, he added, “The chemistry I had with Kathleen Turner was so strong, audiences have been certain for years that we were in a relationship together while making the film. We both denied it through Romancing The Stone, Jewel of the Nile, War of the Roses, and even while doing press a few years ago for The Kominsky Method.”Michael Douglas reveals how affair with Kathleen turner beganGoing on to reveal the “official story” about their relationship and the reason he 'lied' about the same, he shared, "Yes, we confessed, we had amazing chemistry. Yes, we were both, as Kathleen said, ‘terrible flirts,’ and yes, we were both tempted, but nothing ever happened between us. That was a lie. It was a lie meant to protect my wife and son, a lie we told the world for 40 years.”According to Douglas, the relationship developed during production as the two actors spent increasing amounts of time together.“The truth is that during the production of Romancing the Stone, Kathleen and I fell hard for each other and began a relationship. It wasn’t a fly-by night affair; it grew naturally from how closely we were working together, how much pressure we were under, how much we respected and cared for one another, and how attracted we were to each other. Like every other guy in the world at the time, I was knocked sideways by Kathleen…,” he wrote.Why Michael Douglas and Kathleen Turner ended their relationshipDouglas revealed that the relationship eventually came to an end after Diandra visited the set with their then-five-year-old son, Cameron.“Even though Diandra and I were having major problems in our relationship, we had our own son to think about. My parents’ divorce had really hurt me as a child, and Cameron was right about the same age I was when my parents split. After that visit, Kathleen and I ended things, and I went back to Diandra. I did it for Cameron, but we shouldn’t have gotten back together. After that first split it was never the same between us ever again,” Douglas wrote.Douglas and Turner went on to reunite professionally in 'The Jewel of the Nile' and 'The War of the Roses', continuing to work together despite their past relationship.Kathleen Turner reacts to Michael Douglas’ revelationFollowing the buzz about the big revelation, the actress shared her candid reaction with People. “Good heavens what a fuss about something 40 years ago!” she said, and went on to add, “I love Michael and I look forward to enjoying the book.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
